commit: see git log of the branch (this file is committed with the work)

requirements.notes: E1 alone fits three domains on real data: content_selection (KuaiRand random exposure, KuaiRand standard logs, MIND), watch_duration (KuaiRand), browsing_frequency (KuaiRand return and sessions).

content_consumption_fitted is true (content_consumption@1, identified under KuaiRand random exposure). randomized_commercial_response_fitted needs E2's randomised commercial-response model registered in docs/v5/calibration/models/ (domain advertising_response or purchase_behavior, identification randomized_controlled_trial); until it is merged the F.2 test fails, and so does every requirement whose test file is test_gate_F.py.
six held-out reports (JSON + Markdown); the gate test recomputes each E1 model's held-out primary metric from the verified data and the checkpoint.
every model is compared with two simple baselines on the same held-out split, with a user-cluster bootstrap interval of the difference.
ECE (15 bins), Brier, reliability tables; PIT uniformity and interval coverage for watch time; count calibration by predicted decile for sessions.
six checkpoints (NumPy npz without pickle, each < 1 MB) with SHA-256 in model cards; load verifies hashes; tamper detection tested.

two datasets (kuairand_pure, mind_small) with SHA-256 per file, schema, licence and full provenance; the criterion asks for 3, which E2's datasets (registered through datasets.register from a calibration/datasets_<x>.py module) supply after merging.
each card and report states what the simulator may and may not infer (population, platform, period, ranges, identification).
a model counts only if it cites a registered, checksummed, non-synthetic dataset; synthetic_only_domains = 0.

important mechanisms are computed: mechanisms named by fitted models, 4.0 behavioural mechanisms, and every kernel module a v5 behaviour package registers; B, C and others must add FIDELITY_REGISTER.md rows for their modules or SP-5.4 fails.

the plan was committed (d6f4767) before any fit; fitting refuses an uncommitted or modified plan; the test checks plan hash, commit order, metrics and candidates, and that no kept model is worse than a baseline.
